subject: History
description: Haryanka and Nanda dynasties of Magadha — pre-Mauryan rulers; Bimbisara, Ajatashatru, Mahapadma Nanda, Dhana Nanda; capitals, conquests, contacts with Buddha-Mahavira.

questions.stem: Who was the founder of the HARYANKA dynasty of Magadha?
questions.explanation: BIMBISARA (r. ~544-492 BCE) founded the Haryanka dynasty after consolidating Magadha (modern Bihar). He was a contemporary of both BUDDHA (Gautama Siddhartha) and MAHAVIRA (Vardhamana). MAJOR ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) Made Rajgir (Rajagriha) the capital, with its 5 hills providing natural fortification. (2) Expanded Magadha through MARRIAGE ALLIANCES — wives from Kosala (Mahakosala's daughter), Vaishali (Lichchhavi princess Chellana), Punjab (Madra princess) — giving him diplomatic + dowry territories. (3) ANNEXED ANGA (eastern Bihar) — first to do so. (4) Patronized Buddha — donated Veluvana (Bamboo Grove) monastery. SUCCESSION DRAMA: BIMBISARA was IMPRISONED AND KILLED by his own son AJATASHATRU (~492 BCE) — a notorious patricide noted in Buddhist Pali texts. EXAM ANGLE: Bimbisara as 'founder of imperial Magadha' is a high-frequency PYQ — appears in CGL, UPSC Prelims, and NDA at least 1× per cycle. EXAMINER MINDSET: testing the FOUNDATION CHRONOLOGY of pre-Mauryan India.

questions.stem: AJATASHATRU is best known for which two military innovations?
questions.explanation: AJATASHATRU (r. ~492-460 BCE) used two innovative weapons in his wars against Kosala and the Vaishali Lichchhavis: (1) MAHASHILAKANTAKA — a giant catapult that hurled large stones (an early siege engine). (2) RATHAMUSALA — a chariot fitted with rotating blades or 'mace-wheels' that mowed down infantry as it rolled. These tools, plus diplomacy, enabled Ajatashatru to defeat the Lichchhavi confederacy after a 16-year war. ACHIEVEMENTS: (1) Annexed Kashi (Varanasi) from his Kosalan grandfather Prasenjit. (2) Defeated Vaishali after splitting the confederacy via spies. (3) Convened the FIRST BUDDHIST COUNCIL at Rajagriha (~483 BCE, just after Buddha's death) — recorded the Sutta and Vinaya Pitakas. PERSONAL: Buddhist texts call him remorseful for killing Bimbisara; converted to Buddhism. SUCCESSORS: Udayin (founded PATALIPUTRA on the confluence of Ganga, Son, Gandak — strategic riverine trade hub). PYQ FREQUENCY: 1-2 Magadha Qs per UPSC/SSC paper. EXAMINER MINDSET: testing knowledge of innovative pre-Mauryan war-tech and diplomatic-warfare hybrid.

questions.stem: Who founded the city of PATALIPUTRA, future capital of multiple empires?
questions.explanation: UDAYIN (Udayabhadra), son of Ajatashatru, founded PATALIPUTRA (c. 460 BCE) at the confluence of Ganga, Son, and (then) Gandak rivers — a strategic position controlling east-west and north-south river commerce. The site replaced Rajgir as Magadhan capital. SUBSEQUENT CAPITAL ROLE: Pataliputra was the seat of (1) Nanda dynasty, (2) Mauryan empire (Chandragupta, Bindusara, Ashoka), (3) Sunga, (4) Gupta empire (Chandragupta I, II, Samudragupta), and (5) Pala (briefly). MODERN: today's PATNA (Bihar capital) sits on the same site. ARCHAEOLOGICAL: Megasthenes (Greek ambassador to Chandragupta Maurya) described Pataliputra as a city ~14.5 km long, 2.4 km wide, fortified with 64 gates and 570 towers (Indica). ETYMOLOGY: 'Putra' = son, with various theories: 'son of Patali' (a tree/plant) or 'son of Patali-grama' (an older village). EXAM ANGLE: Pataliputra-related questions are EXTREMELY HIGH-FREQUENCY in UPSC (it covers 4-5 dynasties), SSC, NDA. EXAMINER MINDSET: testing knowledge of dynasty-capital chronology — a foundational exam skill.

questions.stem: MAHAPADMA NANDA, founder of the Nanda dynasty, is historically notable for being:
questions.explanation: MAHAPADMA NANDA (r. ~345-321 BCE) overthrew the Shishunagas (successors to Haryankas) and founded the NANDA dynasty. UNIQUE: he was a SHUDRA (or possibly a barber's son) — making him the first NON-KSHATRIYA emperor of north India, defying the Vedic varna hierarchy. He's called 'Ekarat' (sole sovereign) in Puranas — the first to bring all of north India under one rule. CONQUESTS: subjugated Kalinga (modern Odisha — see Hathigumpha inscription of Kharavela mentioning Nanda's irrigation canal there); Kosala; Avanti; possibly Mysore. WEALTH: legendary — Greek sources call them 'Nava Nandas' (nine Nandas) and describe vast treasury. ARMY: Plutarch says Dhana Nanda (last Nanda king) had 200,000 infantry, 80,000 cavalry, 8,000 chariots, 6,000 war elephants — terrified Alexander's troops, leading to the famous mutiny on the Beas River (326 BCE). SUCCESSOR: Dhana Nanda was overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya (with Chanakya/Kautilya's strategy, ~321 BCE). PYQ ANGLE: 'first Shudra emperor' is a perennial CGL/UPSC test question.

questions.stem: DHANA NANDA, last Nanda emperor, was overthrown by:
questions.explanation: CHANDRAGUPTA MAURYA, with the strategic mentorship of CHANAKYA (also Kautilya/Vishnugupta), overthrew DHANA NANDA around 321 BCE — founding the MAURYAN EMPIRE. The story is dramatized in 'Mudra-Rakshasa' (a Sanskrit play by Vishakhadatta, 4th century CE). MOTIVATION (per legend): Chanakya was insulted at Dhana Nanda's court — he vowed to overthrow the dynasty. He recruited young Chandragupta (whose origins are debated — possibly a Maurya/Moriya tribe member, possibly low-born) and trained him at Taxila in statecraft + military strategy. The pair then waged a guerrilla campaign from the northwest, gradually capturing territory. SOURCES: Greek (Justin's Epitome calls Chandragupta 'Sandrocottos'), Buddhist (Mahavamsa, Dipavamsa), Jain (Parishishtaparvan), and Puranas all confirm this overthrow. CHRONOLOGY: Mauryan rule 321-185 BCE; Chandragupta abdicated in old age, became a Jain monk, fasted to death at Sravanabelagola (Karnataka). EXAM-FAVORITE: 'Maurya foundation date 321 BCE' + Chanakya's role appears in UPSC, SSC, RRB ancient-history sections virtually every cycle.

questions.stem: Which Magadhan king convened the FIRST BUDDHIST COUNCIL at Rajagriha?

options.option_text: Ashoka the Great of Mauryan empire

questions.explanation: FIRST BUDDHIST COUNCIL — convened at RAJAGRIHA (Rajgir, Bihar), c. 483 BCE, soon after Buddha's death (parinirvana). Patron: AJATASHATRU. President: Mahakasyapa. ~500 monks attended; goal was to compile Buddha's teachings. OUTPUTS: (1) Vinaya Pitaka (rules of monastic discipline) — recited by Upali. (2) Sutta Pitaka (Buddha's discourses) — recited by Ananda. (Abhidhamma added later.) FOUR BUDDHIST COUNCILS — full list: 1st: Rajagriha (483 BCE) — Ajatashatru patron. 2nd: Vaishali (383 BCE) — Kalashoka patron; led to schism (Sthaviravada vs Mahasanghika). 3rd: Pataliputra (250 BCE) — ASHOKA patron; finalized the Tripitaka, sent missionaries (Mahinda to Sri Lanka, etc.). 4th: Kashmir (~78 CE) — KANISHKA patron; led to Mahayana-Hinayana split. PYQ EXTREME-HIGH-FREQUENCY: 'patron of Buddhist council' appears in UPSC Prelims 1-2× per year, also in CGL/CHSL. EXAMINER MINDSET: tests cross-mapping of dynasty + religious patronage + chronology.

questions.stem: What was the CAPITAL of Magadha under BIMBISARA before it shifted to Pataliputra?

options.option_text: Rajagriha, the city of five hills

questions.explanation: RAJAGRIHA (Rajgir, Nalanda district, Bihar) was the capital of Magadha under Bimbisara and Ajatashatru. Surrounded by FIVE HILLS — Vaibhar, Vipula, Saptaparni, Ratnagiri, and Udaygiri — making it naturally fortified, hence its name 'Giri-vraja' (girdle of hills). HISTORICAL SIGNIFICANCE: (1) Buddha frequently visited and preached here; the Saptaparni cave hosted the First Buddhist Council. (2) Mahavira spent ~14 monsoons here. (3) Bimbisara built the famous 'Cyclopean Wall' — one of the oldest known stone fortifications in India (~5th century BCE). MOVE TO PATALIPUTRA: under Udayin (~460 BCE), capital shifted to the strategically superior riverine site. MODERN RAJGIR: tourist circuit includes hot springs (Brahmakund), Vulture's Peak (Gridhrakuta — Buddha's preaching mount), Saptaparni cave, ancient university Nalanda nearby. UNESCO TENTATIVE LIST: Rajgir + Nalanda + Vikramshila are bid for World Heritage status. PYQ ANGLE: 'Magadha capital chronology' (Rajgir → Pataliputra) appears in UPSC, SSC ancient-history every 2 cycles.
